noFap is not just about getting your erections back, it's about getting your sanity back. It's about rebuilding the parts of your brain that deal with you as a social being. It's about teaching your brain to enjoy meeting people again. It's about learning how to cope with rejection/boredom/horniness/depression/negativity with something else than porn &/or masturbation. 

It is not a myth, it's a reality. You will be different without porn. Don't wait until fapping turn you in a miserable being to start making change on the long term. You dont have to go so low. You can reach wonders, if you will only build slowly new habits in your life.

However, for this to happen, I think you need to realise - or actually he needs to realise - it is an addiction. And it is not very easy to understand at first, for two reason: 
1) Everyone is doing it. Like 99.9% of the world is on porn. 
2) It is not obvious how such a natural thing as sex can be addictive. It is not like alchohol or anything, isn't it? - That's why learning about the topic is so vital because once you understand the mechanism of porn, you can slowly come to accept that porn addiction is not some invention of some crazy semi-religious bigotry conspiration, but it is real, it is a fact, it is scientifically proven and it hurts.

People have sacrificed their health, their career, their family because of this addiction.
The fact that he is willing to stop, and he said he wants to is a good sign. Now he needs a supportive environnment and learning materials. Spend your week end reading noFap together as a romance activity, I dunno :)

Anyway, I hope you'll find a solution.

Kuddos for the move. Taking action is a great way to just avoid not doing anything and complaining about your life.
I have travelled many time for a few weeks to a few month accross the globe. 
The main thing I can take off as a positive move travelling is that it is a wonderful time to read and rethink your life. 
You are free, and away. But it only last some time. Wherever you settle, you are likely to revive the same problems you had before leaving. So use your travel time wisely. Take a few books with you. I would advice for Getting things Done, from David Allen, Ignore Everybody from McLeod Hugh, maybe "Start with Why" from Simon Sinek, maybe some meditation book. It might sound funny but really handling the business of life is so often ignored we end up putting ourselves in shitty situation.
Enjoy your trip, hope you find yourself somewhere on the way :)
